summary: Govern feature worktree lifecycle and provide a loopback-only hub for configured projects, Git-backed worktree status, feature progress, and canonical local artifacts.
plain_summary: People can see local projects and work copies, understand what needs attention, and open the right progress view or project document.
gating: Work checkpoints in order. Within a checkpoint, the gates run in order: behavior, then ui, then review. A checkpoint is "passed" only when every gate is "passed" or "n/a". Do not start checkpoint N+1 until checkpoint N has passed.

checkpoints.title: Discover projects and classify their worktrees
checkpoints.simple: Trust evidence for each work copy
checkpoints.goal: Read-only discovery scans only configured project roots, lists each discovered repository's Git-registered worktrees using its configured worktree root, and maps explicit Git/checkpoint evidence plus verified pre-worktree approvals to the approved lifecycle filters.

plain.what: People can see local work copies with a status supported by evidence.
plain.why: Missing or conflicting records must not make uncertain work look active or finished.
plain.check: Filter the list and inspect waiting, active, blocked, closed, and unknown work.

tasks: src/shared-worktree.ts: expose a read-only repository-root-scoped worktree inventory for the hub while preserving the existing `ai-eng worktree list` contract and its local-only safety checks.

src/workspace/discovery.ts: find repositories only beneath canonical configured roots, reject symlink escapes, surface unreadable roots, and after finding a repository include only its Git-registered worktrees, including paths under that repository's configured `[git].worktrees_dir` even when that directory is outside the search root.

src/workspace/status.ts: derive all, needs-review, in-progress, blocked, closed, and unknown from Git plus a matching valid checkpoint/lifecycle record. Needs-review means a valid `approval-before-start` projection or awaiting-plan/app-review phase; in-progress means implementation or ready-to-merge; blocked requires explicit blocked lifecycle or Git conflict evidence. Dirty status is detail, not proof of activity. Build closed history only from a checkpoint on local main with complete gates and Git merge evidence, and classify missing, legacy, stale, malformed, detached, prunable, or contradictory evidence as unknown.

src/workspace/api.ts and src/workspace/server.ts: add read-only project/worktree/history endpoints; refresh only on startup or explicit user request, never by continuous polling, and keep per-project Git or checkpoint read failures in the response for visible UI handling.

tests/workspace-discovery.spec.ts and tests/workspace-server.spec.ts: use temporary Git repositories to prove configured-root boundaries, custom worktree roots, Git registration, all six status buckets, and unknown precedence for missing or conflicting evidence.
tests/worktree-lifecycle.spec.ts: retain and extend regression coverage for the existing CLI worktree inventory if its shared read-only helper changes.
acceptance: Repository discovery never scans outside configured canonical roots; worktrees are included only when Git registers them to an in-scope repository, respecting that repository's configured worktree directory. A verified pre-worktree approval may appear from its explicit lifecycle projection.
Every lifecycle label is backed by Git and a matching valid checkpoint; dirty work alone never means active, and missing, stale, malformed, or contradictory evidence is Unknown.
Needs-review, in-progress, and blocked map only to explicit approval phases, implementation/ready-to-merge phases, or a blocked phase/Git conflict; dirty files alone do not imply any of them.

Closed history requires a matching checkpoint on local main, Git proof that the feature reached local main, no registered feature worktree, and complete checkpoint gates; lack of a live worktree alone is not proof of closure.
Project and worktree inventory is read-only, refreshes at startup or user request only, and reports partial read errors instead of hiding them.
